description: This case study is a six-page extended abstract for the 2026 CHI conference on how farmers maintain distributed solar irrigation systems. The authors studied grid-connected solar irrigation schemes that pay farmers to feed energy to the grid and found that farmers face multiple challenges but devise strategies, including using WhatsApp to share daily generation data with peers and to compare performance across installations to spot anomalies. They argue that messaging platforms act as informal digital infrastructure for collective sensemaking around distributed energy systems, and outline implications for designing agricultural energy technologies with peer comparison and community-driven maintenance and directions for integrating this with formal monitoring tools and citizen science. Coverage: schemes in the study region, which the abstract does not name. Access: free preprint; licence CC-BY-4.0 (the paper, as linked on its arXiv abstract page). Caveats: a short qualitative study, with no quantitative performance data. It informs agent-based and operations models of pump maintenance and uptime in distributed irrigation energy systems, and lists no linked catalogue records.
